examples.question_text: The region between $y=2x+1$, the $x$-axis, $x=1$ and $x=2$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.

Find the exact volumes formed by rotating these regions about the $x$-axis:
a. Between $y=x^2$, the $x$-axis, $x=1$ and $x=3$.
b. Between $y=\sqrt{x}$, the $x$-axis, $x=2$ and $x=6$.
examples.solution_text:
a. Square the radius before integrating.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_1^3(x^2)^2\,dx\\&=\pi\int_1^3x^4\,dx\\&=\pi\left[\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_1^3\\&=\frac{242\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^3\end{aligned}$
b. Squaring removes the square root.
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_2^6(\sqrt{x})^2\,dx\\&=\pi\int_2^6x\,dx\\&=\pi\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_2^6\\&=16\pi\ \text{units}^3\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The region between $y=\dfrac{4}{x}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=2$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.
The region between $y=e^{3x}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=1$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.
The region between $y=\dfrac1{\sqrt{x}}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=3$ to $x=9$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.
The region bounded by $y=\tan x$, the $x$-axis and $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.
The region between $y=\cos x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the exact volume.

examples.solution_text:
Find the intercepts.
$\begin{aligned}x^3-9x&=0\\x(x-3)(x+3)&=0\\x&=-3,\ 0,\ 3\end{aligned}$
The radius is $|x^3-9x|$. Its square is even, so integrate from $0$ to $3$ and double.
$\begin{aligned}V&=2\pi\int_0^3(x^3-9x)^2\,dx\\&=2\pi\int_0^3(x^6-18x^4+81x^2)\,dx\\&=2\pi\left[\frac{x^7}{7}-\frac{18x^5}{5}+27x^3\right]_0^3\\&=2\pi\left(\frac{2187}{7}-\frac{4374}{5}+729\right)\\&=\frac{11664\pi}{35}\ \text{units}^3\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The region between $y=\sqrt{16-x^2}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=4$ is rotated about the $x$-axis, forming a hemisphere. Find its exact volume by integration.

A vessel is modelled by rotating the region between $y=2+\sqrt{x}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=4$ about the $x$-axis. Each coordinate unit represents $1$ cm. Find its exact capacity in cubic centimetres.
examples.solution_text:
Expand the whole squared radius, including the cross term.
$\begin{aligned}(2+\sqrt{x})^2&=4+4\sqrt{x}+x\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^4(4+4x^{1/2}+x)\,dx\\&=\pi\left[4x+\frac83x^{3/2}+\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^4\\&=\pi\left(16+\frac{64}{3}+8\right)\\&=\frac{136\pi}{3}\ \text{cm}^3\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: π∫₁²(2x+1)² dx = π[(2x+1)³/6]₁² = π(125−27)/6 = 49π/3 cubic units.
Part a: π∫₁³x⁴ dx = π(243−1)/5 = 242π/5 cubic units. Part b: π∫₂⁶x dx = π(36−4)/2 = 16π cubic units.
π∫₁²16x⁻² dx = π[−16/x]₁² = π(−8+16) = 8π cubic units. The mapped rational-radius source uses the same negative-power integration method.
Squaring e^(3x) gives e^(6x); π∫₀¹e^(6x) dx = π[e^(6x)/6]₀¹ = π(e⁶−1)/6 cubic units.
The squared radius is 1/x. π∫₃⁹dx/x = π(ln 9−ln 3) = π ln 3 cubic units.
